fact_label: Compulsory schooling applies to foreign-resident children
notes: Access is confirmed: a 2005 Cabinet Resolution guarantees free basic education to any child regardless of nationality or legal status, and the Ministry of Education mandated from the 2025 academic year that every school under its supervision accept foreign-national or unregistered children. Stated as 'Not stated' rather than guessed.

Legal since a 2004 ministerial regulation ('the right to basic education by the family') recognized the family itself as an educational institution — a genuine, two-decade-old statutory basis, not informal tolerance. fact_label: Long-Term Resident (LTR) Work-from-Thailand Professional / Highly-Skilled Professional 0% foreign-sourced income tax exemption
notes: Long-Term Resident (LTR) holders (Royal Decree No. 743) are the only visa-holder group with a statutory foreign-income tax exemption; the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) carries no equivalent exemption. New row, 2026-07-18 ([specialist]), thinnest-3-criteria backfill — this criterion (income-viability) had zero fact rows anywhere in derived/facts/TH.jsonl before, despite being a scored criterion (3/5, all three locations) whose reasoning currently lives only in narrative form under the visa-legal-pathway-ease criterion's own facts. Real, distinct legal-and-economic mechanism, not a restatement: a Long-Term Resident (LTR) holder's foreign-sourced income earned in a prior year and remitted to Thailand is exempt from Thai personal income tax by statute — a materially different tax exposure than a Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) holder's, whose foreign income becomes taxable on remittance once they cross the 180-day tax-residency threshold, with no equivalent statutory carve-out.

fact_label: Foreign-sourced income taxation on remittance — 2024 rule, 2026 proposed softening
value_raw: Since 2024, a Thai tax resident (180+ days/year) who remits foreign-sourced income to Thailand in the year it is earned owes Thai personal income tax on it, regardless of visa type (except LTR's statutory exemption above). A Revenue Department proposal, not yet formally enacted as of this research, would exempt foreign-sourced income from tax if remitted within the year earned or the following year, intended to apply from the 2026 tax year onward.
notes: New row, 2026-07-18 ([specialist]), genuinely new research (not extraction) — the specific 2024-rule/2026-proposal mechanics weren't previously in any Thailand fact row, only the general 180-day tax-residency trigger was. Directly relevant to AI/remote-work economics: a foreign-employer-paid freelancer or contractor on the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) (see TH:dtv-income-type-requirement-passive) is the archetype this rule binds hardest, since DTV income is by definition foreign-sourced and DTV holders who stay 180+ days become tax residents on the same terms as anyone else. Held at Medium confidence and 'improving' trajectory since the 2026 softening is a proposal, not yet enacted law — worth re-checking once/if it's formally enacted.

fact_label: Remote work for a foreign employer/clients — legality under the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)
value_raw: Legal under the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) specifically: remote work for foreign employers/clients is explicitly permitted; a Thai work permit, or any work for a Thai company or local income, is explicitly prohibited
notes: New row, 2026-07-18 ([specialist]), thinnest-3-criteria backfill — mechanical extraction of already-sourced visa-legal.md prose (Option 1's "Work rights" bullet) into its own fact row under the income-viability criterion, which previously had none; the underlying fact already existed under visa-legal-pathway-ease's own facts but was never given an income-viability-scoped row of its own. Directly names the legal mechanism behind how AI-adjacent/remote-freelance income specifically plays out here: a foreign client relationship (including AI-tool-mediated freelance/consulting work billed to non-Thai clients) is the legally clean shape; taking on a Thai client or Thai-sourced income is not, regardless of visa route held. If a real need for a joined work-rights category emerges later, that would be a fresh proposal to extend the schema, not a re-add of this unregistered token.
